findings.location: Proof 2.1, paragraph beginning “The peripheral action has a translation line and no fixed vertex.”
findings.evidence: The proof asserts that the midpoint inverse image is a locally flat surface after only avoiding midpoint values at domain vertices. A nonzero affine direction in the least incident simplex does not establish the required local 2-manifold links at lower-dimensional simplices; sheets may branch along a domain edge. No relative equivariant PL transversality or link verification is supplied before later smoothing and compression steps use this set as a surface. The proof needs such a construction fixing the prescribed boundary collar, or an explicit local-link verification before smoothing. This assigned consumer uses the supplier's resulting surface to establish the boundary-slope conclusion.
